chapters.screenText: Set one ISSM solver limit, review it, then launch explicitly.
chapters.screenWhy: Use the reviewed BYO workflow for one native ISSM solver change.
chapters.expectedResult: Example: canonical SquareIceShelf; stressbalance iteration cap 120.
chapters.title: Goal and prerequisites
instructions: Open CryoLauncher with a verified BYO AWS connection. Configure your MATLAB license and connect the same-owner Connector.
Choose Cloud and ISSM SquareIceShelf. This guide changes only the stressbalance maximum-iteration setting.
chapters.note: Auto-config prepares a configuration; Create plan and Apply to configuration do not submit a native job.
chapters.why: Use the reviewed BYO workflow for one native ISSM solver change.

chapters.screenText: Describe the change: Set stressbalance max iterations to 120.
chapters.screenWhy: A narrow request makes the proposed change easy to verify.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep the model, example and Cloud execution mode.
chapters.title: 1. Describe a single change
instructions: Choose Auto-config · Beta.
Enter exactly: Set stressbalance max iterations to 120.
chapters.why: A narrow request makes the proposed change easy to verify.

chapters.screenText: Choose Create plan. Read the proposed value of 120.
chapters.screenWhy: A plan proposes a change; it does not start the solver.
chapters.title: 2. Create and review the proposal
instructions: Choose Create plan.
Review the Stressbalance max iterations row. Proposed must be 120; retain ISSM · SquareIceShelf · Cloud.
chapters.why: A plan proposes a change; it does not start the solver.

chapters.screenText: Apply the reviewed 120 limit to the launch form.
chapters.screenWhy: Apply only after confirming 120 and the retained experiment.
chapters.title: 3. Apply the reviewed setting
instructions: Scroll to the proposal and choose Apply to configuration.
Wait for Configuration updated and 1 setting changed.
chapters.note: The accepted staged helper later set md.stressbalance.maxiter = 120 before the native solve.
chapters.why: Apply only after confirming 120 and the retained experiment.

chapters.screenText: Choose Review in Advanced to inspect the native controls.
chapters.screenWhy: The native form is where you review execution controls.
chapters.expectedResult: Continue to the normal launch form.
chapters.title: 4. Return to the native form
instructions: Choose Review in Advanced to inspect the native controls.
Review the existing model and run controls before launching.
chapters.why: The native form is where you review execution controls.

chapters.screenWhy: The change should not select a different scientific example.
chapters.title: 5. Check the retained example
instructions: In Experiment confirm Model ISSM and Examples SquareIceShelf.
chapters.note: Canonical Square.par remains unchanged: hmax 1000 m and hmin 300 m.
chapters.why: The change should not select a different scientific example.

chapters.screenText: Confirm Action Run and target runme.m.
chapters.screenWhy: runme.m retains the canonical scientific entrypoint.
chapters.expectedResult: The native canonical entrypoint is retained.
chapters.title: 6. Check the run target
instructions: Keep Action Run and Run target runme.m.
chapters.note: The recorded case retained two requested MPI processes and the qualified image pin.
chapters.why: runme.m retains the canonical scientific entrypoint.

chapters.screenText: Read the native review: ISSM · SquareIceShelf.
chapters.screenWhy: Review before submitting so the new run uses the intended example.
chapters.expectedResult: Check the reviewed model and example before submission.
chapters.title: 7. Review the native cloud plan
instructions: Open Review & Launch. Confirm ISSM and SquareIceShelf.
Review your resource and time-limit settings and the cost estimate in your own account.
chapters.note: The accepted run used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. An estimate is not an invoice or a spending cap.
chapters.why: Review before submitting so the new run uses the intended example.

chapters.screenText: Scroll to Infrastructure. Check that every row is Ready.
chapters.screenWhy: Storage, image, license and compute must be ready before submission.
chapters.expectedResult: Account, storage, image and compute must be ready.
chapters.title: 8. Check readiness
instructions: In the expanded review, scroll to Infrastructure.
Check Account, Storage, Container image and Compute readiness.
chapters.note: Read the review before the separate explicit launch action.
chapters.why: Storage, image, license and compute must be ready before submission.

chapters.screenText: Choose Launch cloud run only after the final review.
chapters.screenWhy: This explicit action starts the native cloud execution.
chapters.expectedResult: This explicit action submits the native job.
chapters.title: 9. Submit explicitly
instructions: Scroll to the bottom of the review. Read the final notice.
Choose Launch cloud run. Stay on the page while staging begins.
chapters.note: Create plan and Apply did not submit this job.
chapters.why: This explicit action starts the native cloud execution.

chapters.screenText: Wait for the new SquareIceShelf run to submit.
chapters.screenWhy: Follow the new run before inspecting its outputs.
chapters.expectedResult: The current run changes from staging to submitting.
chapters.title: 10. Follow the selected run
instructions: Check that the new Cloud run names SquareIceShelf.
Follow this selected run until Completed; startup and model execution are separate periods.
chapters.note: Recorded startup 212.717 s; Batch task 41.369 s; total submission-to-stop 254.086 s.
chapters.why: Follow the new run before inspecting its outputs.

chapters.screenText: Open Results. Choose StressbalanceSolution and Vel.
chapters.screenWhy: The selected field must belong to the completed run.
chapters.expectedResult: The completed native result contains 91 nodal velocity values.
chapters.title: 11. Select the native field
instructions: For the completed Auto-config run open View results or Results.
Select StressbalanceSolution and field Vel.
chapters.note: The result belongs to the selected run, rather than the current experiment controls on the left.
chapters.why: The selected field must belong to the completed run.

chapters.screenWhy: Render updates the displayed field; it does not rerun the solver.
chapters.title: 12. Render the field
instructions: Choose Render after selecting Vel.
Read the field summary and colorbar; the accepted mesh has 91 vertices and 148 triangles.
chapters.why: Render updates the displayed field; it does not rerun the solver.

chapters.screenText: Choose Download results. Wait for the new archive link.
chapters.screenWhy: Package the mesh, fields, figure and runtime provenance together.
chapters.expectedResult: A fresh results_bundle link appears for this run.
chapters.title: 13. Prepare the result archive
instructions: Scroll below the rendered field and choose Download results.
Wait for a newly prepared results_bundle link. Keep the run selected while packaging.
chapters.why: Package the mesh, fields, figure and runtime provenance together.

chapters.screenText: Choose the fresh results_bundle link to save it.
chapters.screenWhy: The fresh link saves the archive prepared for this run.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep the native outputs and runtime provenance together.
chapters.title: 14. Save the result archive
instructions: Choose the fresh download link. Save the ZIP with your run record.
The accepted archive contains the neutral mesh, native fields, exact figure and runtime/RNG provenance.
chapters.why: The fresh link saves the archive prepared for this run.

chapters.screenText: Inspect the saved native velocity figure.
chapters.screenWhy: The colorbar and solver record explain the result in physical units.
chapters.expectedResult: ISSM converged in 23 iterations, below both caps of 100 and 120.
chapters.title: 15. Interpret this result
instructions: Open figures/StressbalanceSolution_Vel.png from the saved archive.
This recorded solve converged in 23 iterations; 120 is an upper limit, not a request for 120 iterations.
chapters.note: Actual runtime: MATLAB R2024b Update 7; ISSM 2026.1. The canonical domain is 1000 km × 1000 km.
chapters.why: The colorbar and solver record explain the result in physical units.

chapters.screenText: Compare the retained mesh and fields with the Basic result.
chapters.screenWhy: Convergence below both caps explains this unchanged recorded result.
chapters.expectedResult: For this changed-cap case, every compared numeric value was exactly equal.
chapters.title: 16. Read the qualification
instructions: The staged override and native log prove that 120 was applied before solve.
The mesh, Pressure, Vel, Vx, Vy and iteration count exactly matched the accepted Basic retake.
chapters.note: This is one changed-cap comparison, consistent with convergence below either cap; it is not a general accuracy or reproducibility claim.
chapters.why: Convergence below both caps explains this unchanged recorded result.
